results.evidence: BroadcastSummary shows a 'Move to draft' button that calls revertBroadcastToDraft, which does `hogFlowsPartialUpdate(..., { status: 'draft' })` and `actions.saveBroadcastFinished(updated)`. The `isReadOnly` selector is `!!broadcast && broadcast.status !== 'draft'`, so once status becomes 'draft' the wizard is editable again. The scheduler firing only for active workflows is unchanged surrounding infrastructure (author summary: 'which is what the scheduler checks before firing'); no code in the diff contradicts this.

`canRevertScheduledBroadcast` returns false unless `broadcast?.status !== 'active'` fails (i.e. excludes drafts), and `const hasUnsentSchedule = (broadcast.schedules ?? []).some((schedule) => schedule.status !== 'completed'); if (!hasUnsentSchedule) { return false }` — an immediate-send broadcast has no schedules (empty array → false) and a completed one-time schedule also yields false, so the control is withheld in both cases.

For scheduled/recurring launches the backend deletes-and-recreates: `if replace_existing: HogFlowSchedule.objects.filter(...).delete()` then creates with `status: ACTIVE`. But for immediate sends the launch action does: `if (values.scheduleMode === 'now') { await hogFlowsBatchJobsCreate(...); lemonToast.success('Broadcast is sending') }` with no call to delete/replace any existing schedule, so a broadcast relaunched with 'now' after previously having a (possibly paused) schedule leaves that schedule behind, contradicting 'Launching with immediate send likewise leaves no leftover schedule behind.'

The code activates the broadcast before creating/replacing the schedule: `activated = await hogFlowsPartialUpdate(projectId, broadcastId, { status: 'active' })` runs first, and only afterward (in the `else` branch) does `await hogFlowsSchedulesCreate(projectId, broadcastId, { ...schedule, replace_existing: true })` run. If the process were interrupted between these two calls (e.g. tab closed) rather than throwing a catchable JS exception, the broadcast would remain live with the stale/paused schedule — the opposite of 'only marked live after the schedule replacement has completed'. The try/catch compensation revert-to-draft is a best-effort fallback, not an ordering that prevents the live-with-stale-schedule window, and the catch itself admits failure can leave it 'still active but has nothing scheduled.'

`canRevertScheduledBroadcast` only checks `broadcast?.status`, schedule completion, and in-flight batch job statuses (`IN_FLIGHT_BATCH_JOB_STATUSES = new Set(['waiting', 'queued', 'active'])`); it never inspects `broadcast.schedules.length` to withhold the control when there is more than one schedule, and there is no check of workflow/action shape (e.g. verifying trigger/email/exit actions) to withhold it when the wizard can't safely edit the flow.

`onClick={() => LemonDialog.open({ title: 'Move this broadcast back to draft?', description: 'The scheduled send will not go out. You can edit it and launch it again.', primaryButton: { children: 'Move to draft', onClick: () => revertBroadcastToDraft() }, secondaryButton: { children: 'Cancel' } })}` — the revert only fires from the primary button's onClick, so cancelling performs no action.

`revertBroadcastToDraft` only does `await hogFlowsPartialUpdate(..., { status: 'draft' })` then `actions.saveBroadcastFinished(updated)` and `actions.setStep(...)`; there is no call to cancel any batch job/run, and no differentiated messaging — there is no `lemonToast.success` at all on success, and the only toast is `lemonToast.error("Couldn't move the broadcast back to draft: ...")` on failure, with no wording that the broadcast is nonetheless now a draft.

None of the changed files (hog_flow.py schedules action, BroadcastSummary.tsx, broadcastWizardLogic.ts) touch any scheduler/run-creation code path; there is no re-verification of broadcast status immediately before a run is created shown anywhere in the diff.

The frontend builds the replacement schedule payload as only `{ rrule, starts_at, timezone }` with no `variables` field carried from the prior schedule: `const schedule: Partial<HogFlowScheduleApi> = { rrule: ..., starts_at: ..., timezone: values.effectiveTimezone }`. The backend's replace path (`HogFlowSchedule.objects.filter(hog_flow=hog_flow, team=self.team).delete()` then `serializer.save(**save_kwargs)`) also never reads or copies variable overrides from the deleted schedule onto the new one.

result:
Scheduled broadcasts can be moved back to draft from the broadcast summary, and launching replaces any existing schedule with a new active one.

The summary for a live broadcast was read-only until it sent, so a mistaken or unfinished schedule could not be stopped or edited from Broadcasts. The summary now offers “Move to draft” when the workflow is active, still has a schedule that has not completed, and no batch run is in flight. That sets the workflow status to draft, which is what the scheduler checks before firing, and opens the wizard on the first incomplete step (or review).

Relaunch was also silent when it should have sent. Editing a draft’s audience pauses every active schedule, and schedule status is read-only, so a later update cannot turn that pause off. Launch still saved the audience first (which applies that pause) and then created another schedule, leaving the paused row in place. The schedule create call now sends `replace_existing`. In the same transaction the API deletes the workflow’s current schedules and stores the new one as active, so the chosen time is what actually fires.

Tests cover the replace-paused-schedule API behavior and when the move-to-draft action is offered.
